California|website=californiabirthindex.org|publisher=[[California Birth Index]]|access-date=May 28, 2020}} (born August 8, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Al-Faisaly SC (basketball)|Al-Faisaly]] of the [[Jordanian Premier Basketball League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut Huskies]], and earned second-team all-conference honors in the [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) as a sophomore. After he decided to forgo his remaining two years of college eligibility, Hamilton was selected in the second round of the [[2016 NBA draft]] by the [[Denver Nuggets]]. His draft rights later were traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. ==High school career== Hamilton attended [[Crenshaw High School]] in [[Los Angeles, California]], and then [[St. John Bosco High School]] in [[Bellflower, California]]. As a senior, he averaged 20.5 points. 9.0 rebounds, 5.2 assists and 1.3 steals, leading the Braves to a 23–11 record and the California Division II state championship.{{cite web|url=http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/daniel_hamilton_922982.html|title=UConn bio|work=UConnHuskies.com|access-date=October 7, 2016|archive-date=June 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612141405/http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/daniel_hamilton_922982.html|url-status=dead}} ==College career== After graduating high school, Hamilton joined the [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut Huskies]]. As a freshman, he averaged 10.9 points, 7.6 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 31.4 minutes in 35 games and was named the AAC Rookie of Year. He became just the second UConn freshman to finish a season with at least 300 points, 200 rebounds and 100 assists.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/hamilton_160623|title=Thunder Acquires Draft Rights to Hamilton|date=June 23, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 7, 2016}} In a 99–52 blowout of [[Central Connecticut Blue Devils men's basketball|Central Connecticut State]] on December 23, 2015, Hamilton posted a [[triple-double]] with 11 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists, the 10th Husky to record one.{{cite news|title=Hamilton leads UConn over Central Connecticut 99–62|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400816807|access-date=May 8, 2018|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 23, 2015}} In his sophomore season, Hamilton averaged 12.5 points, a conference-best 8.9 rebounds, 4.7 assists, 1.1 steals and 31.9 minutes in 36 games, being named the Most Outstanding Player of the 2016 AAC Championship and was an AAC All-Conference Second Teamer. After leaving UConn, Hamilton was one of two Division I players (the other being LSU's [[Ben Simmons]]) to register more than 450 points, 300 rebounds and 150 assists on the season. ==Professional career== On June 23, 2016, Hamilton was selected with the 56th pick of the [[2016 NBA draft]] by the [[Denver Nuggets]], however, he was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] on draft night. In July, 2016, he joined the Thunder in the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_summerleague_160701|title=Thunder Announces Summer League Roster|date=July 1, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 7, 2016}} ===Oklahoma City Blue (2016–2017)=== On November 3, 2016, he was acquired by the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].{{cite web|url=http://oklahomacity.dleague.nba.com/news/oklahoma-city-blue-announces-training-camp-roster/|title=Oklahoma City Blue Announces Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=November 3, 2016|access-date=November 5, 2016|archive-date=January 15, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170115155159/http://oklahomacity.dleague.nba.com/news/oklahoma-city-blue-announces-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2017–2018)=== On August 3, 2017, Hamilton signed a [[two-way contract]] with the team that acquired him on draft night, the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. As a result, he would split the season between the Thunder and the Blue, their G League affiliate.{{cite news|title=Thunder Signs Daniel Hamilton to Two-Way Contract |url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/hamilton-170803|access-date=August 3, 2017|work=[[Oklahoma City Thunder]]|date=August 3, 2017}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2018–2019)=== On August 20, 2018, Hamilton signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Daniel Hamilton and Alex Poythress|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-daniel-hamilton-and-alex-poythress|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 21, 2018}} On February 8, 2019, Hamilton was waived by the Hawks.{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Request Waivers On Daniel Hamilton|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/atlanta-hawks-request-waivers-daniel-hamilton|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 18, 2019|date=February 8, 2019}} On September 30, 2019, Hamilton was included in the training camp roster of the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|title=View 2019 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/training-camp-roster-2019|date=September 30, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 30, 2019}} Hamilton was later waived by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on October 15, 2019.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Waive Four Players|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/cavs-waive-four-players-191015|date=October 15, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 15, 2019}} ===Mets de Guaynabo (2020)=== On February 1, 2020, he has signed with [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Mets de Guaynabo]] of the [[Baloncesto Ligi|Turkish Super League]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/frutti-extra-bursaspor-signs-daniel-hamilton/|title=Frutti Extra Bursaspor signs Daniel Hamilton|date=July 30, 2020|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 30, 2020}} ===Petkim Spor (2021–2022)=== On November 8, 2021, Hamilton signed with [[Petkim Spor]] of the Turkish [[Basketball Super League]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketfaul.com/haber?haber=97356|title=PETKİM'de bir kayıp, bir transfer|last=|first=|date=November 8, 2021|website=|publisher=basketfaul|language=tr|access-date=November 8, 2021}} He averaged 9.2 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 2.5 assists per game. ===Ionikos Nikaias (2022)=== On February 12, 2022, Hamilton signed with [[Ionikos Nikaias B.C.|Ionikos Nikaias]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] for the rest of the season.{{cite web |title=Daniel Hamilton signs with Ionikos BC |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/daniel-hamilton-signs-with-ionikos-bc/ |website=Sportando |access-date=February 12, 2022 |date=February 12, 2022}} In 9 league games, he averaged a spectacular 18.6 points, 10.4 rebounds, 5.6 assists, and 1.2 steals, playing around 37 minutes per contest and helping the club avoid relegation in the process. ===VEF Rīga (2022)=== On August 15, 2022, Hamilton signed with [[BK VEF Rīga|VEF Rīga]] of the [[Latvian-Estonian Basketball League]].{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/vef-riga-signs-daniel-hamilton/|title=VEF Riga signs Daniel Hamilton|last=|first=|date=August 15, 2022|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 17, 2022}} ===Second stint with Ionikos (2022–2023)=== On November 11, 2022, Hamilton returned to Greece and [[Ionikos Nikaias B.C.|Ionikos]] for the rest of the season.
